name: collect-fragments
summary: Normalize caller-supplied source fragments into a clean, de-duplicated, order-preserving source_fragments list.
description: First node of the report.* chain, ported from the UMA chapter-13 portable MCP runtime's DataProviderLocal (re-scoped from a canned-fixture provider to a real input normalizer). Genuinely reads the `fragments` input and returns `source_fragments`: each fragment trimmed of surrounding whitespace, empty/whitespace-only fragments dropped, case-insensitive exact duplicates dropped (first occurrence kept), original order preserved, and any fragment longer than 2000 characters clipped on a UTF-8 char boundary. Also returns `dropped_count` (how many input fragments were removed) and `status` (`ok`, or `insufficient_data` when nothing survives normalization). No model, network, randomness, or host state dependency: identical input always produces identical output. Built no_std on the shared capability-src/wasi-capability-runtime shim, verified to import only wasi_snapshot_preview1::{fd_read, fd_write, proc_exit}, so it is genuinely executable by Traverse's runtime ABI whitelist. Known limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: de-duplication is exact-match only (after trim, clip, and lowercase) -- near-duplicate fragments that differ by punctuation or wording are both kept, which is correct for a normalizer that must not lose caller intent. Source: capability-src/report-collect-fragments/ in this repo.

use_cases.scenario: As a rollout coordinator, I want three distinct browser/edge/cloud status notes passed straight through in order, so that the rest of the report chain sees exactly the evidence I supplied.

fragments: The browser shell holds recent customer feedback snippets.
An edge cache exposes regional rollout data with low latency.
A cloud record confirms that contract validation reduced incident handoff time.

source_fragments: The browser shell holds recent customer feedback snippets.
An edge cache exposes regional rollout data with low latency.
A cloud record confirms that contract validation reduced incident handoff time.

use_cases.scenario: As a rollout coordinator, I want a fragment list that repeats one note (in a different case) and includes a blank line to come back trimmed and de-duplicated, so that the summary is not skewed by accidental repetition.
As a rollout coordinator, I want an all-blank fragment list to be flagged rather than silently producing an empty report, so that I know to supply real source material.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a `fragments` array of strings; its contents are read and normalized.

postconditions.description: Returns `source_fragments` containing each non-empty input fragment trimmed, clipped to 2000 characters, and de-duplicated case-insensitively with first-seen order preserved; `dropped_count` equals the number of input fragments removed; `status` is `insufficient_data` when `source_fragments` is empty and `ok` otherwise. The same input always produces the same output.

side_effects.description: Produces one deterministic normalized fragment list derived from the provided fragments; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.

authoring.test_evidence: Greenfield no_std capability on capability-src/wasi-capability-runtime; capability-src/report-collect-fragments cargo llvm-cov --summary-only --json: functions=100.00%, lines=100.00%, regions=100.00% (11 #[test] cases covering trim, empty-drop, case-insensitive dedupe, order preservation, char-boundary clip, dedupe-after-clip, all-empty insufficient_data, missing key, end-to-end JSON round-trip, and determinism). Compiled wasm imports verified = wasi_snapshot_preview1::{fd_read, fd_write, proc_exit} only.
